body.p: This Response is to the Non-Final Office Action dated August 29, 2024. The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge Deposit Account 02-1818 for any additional fees which are due and owing. If any such charges are applied, please indicate Attorney Docket No. 3726071.00275 on the account statement.

Claims 1 to 20 are pending in this application and stand rejected. Claims 1 and 11 are in independent form. By this Response, Claims 1 and 11 are amended herein. In view of the amendments and remarks made herein, favorable reconsideration is respectfully requested.

The Office Action (i) objects to the drawings under 37 CFR 1.83(a); (ii) rejects Claims 1 to 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) as allegedly failing to comply with the written description requirement; (iii) rejects Claims 1, 3, 11, and 13 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2008/0139953 to Baker et al. ("Baker"); (iv) rejects Claims 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, 13, 14, and 18 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Baker in view of U.S. Publication No. 2011/0160601 to Wang et al. ("Wang"); (v) rejects Claims 2 and 12 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Baker and Wang in view of U.S. Publication No. 2008/0288026 to Cross et al. ("Cross"); (vi) rejects Claims 5, 6, 15, and 16 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Baker and Wang in view of U.S. Publication No. 2011/0021937 to Hugh et al. ("Hugh"); (vii) rejects Claims 7 and 17 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Baker and Wang in view of U.S. Publication No. 2011/0237924 to McGusty et al. ("McGusty"); and (viii) rejects Claims 9, 10, 19, and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Baker and Wang in view of U.S. Publication No. 2007/0208232 to Kovacs et al. ("Kovacs").

The Office Action objects to the drawings under 37 CFR 1.83(a). Specifically, the Office Action states that "the 'processor' must be shown or the feature(s) canceled from the claim(s)." Office Action 8/29/24 at p. 2. Without acquiescing to the merits of the objection and solely to advance prosecution, Applicant removes the term "processor" from the claims. Thus, Applicant
respectfully submits that the objection to the drawings is moot. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that the objections to the drawings be reconsidered and withdrawn.

The Office Action rejects Claims 1 to 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) as allegedly failing to comply with the written description requirement. Specifically, the Office Action states that "[t]here is no mention of a microcontroller working in concert with a processor." Office Action 8/29/24 at p. 3. Without acquiescing to the merits of the rejection and solely to advance prosecution, Applicant clarifies the claims and removes the language of a "processor." Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 1 to 20 overcome the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a). Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) be reconsidered and withdrawn.

The Office Action rejects Claims 1, 3, 11, and 13 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by Baker. Office Action 8/29/24 at p. 4. However, the cited portions of Baker do not disclose "electrical contacts that protrude from the bottom surface of the housing to connect to a battery to power the microcontroller, wherein the battery is disposed between the microcontroller and skin of a patient" as recited in currently amended Claim 1.

To teach the previously claimed "battery," the Office Action identifies "batteries as per Figure 4." Id.; see Figure 4. However, the cited portions of Baker do not disclose the claimed battery because the battery of Baker is not "disposed between the microcontroller and skin of a patient" as recited in currently amended Claim 1. Figure 2 (reproduced below) of Baker further highlights this failure. As shown in Figure 2, the batteries 204 are not "disposed between the microcontroller and skin of a patient."
Baker, Figure 2.

For the above reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that the cited portions of Baker fail to disclose Claim 1 as amended herein. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of independent Claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 should be reconsidered and withdrawn. Additionally, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 3, which directly depends from independent Claim 1, is also allowable for the reasons given above with respect to Claim 1 and for the additional patentable features recited therein.

Furthermore, Applicant submits that independent Claim 11 includes similar patentable features to those discussed above with respect to independent Claim 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that amended Claim 11 is patentable over Baker for the same reasons as Claim 1. Lastly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 13, which depends directly from independent Claim 11, is also allowable for the reasons given above with respect to Claims 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of independent Claims 11 and 13 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

The Office Action rejects Claims 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, 13, 14, and 18 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Baker in view of Wang. Office Action 8/29/24 at p. 6. For the reasons discussed above, the cited portions of Baker do not disclose "electrical contacts that protrude from the bottom surface of the housing to connect to a battery to power the

microcontroller, wherein the battery is disposed between the microcontroller and skin of a patient" as recited in currently amended Claim 1. The Office Action's citation to Figure 14 of Baker fails to remedy this deficiency.

Namely, the Office Action states that "the processor and housing in 102 is 'over' the battery" in Figure 14. Id. at 7. Even assuming the housing is over the battery (which Applicant does not concede), the battery is not "disposed between the microcontroller and skin of a patient" as recited in currently amended Claim 1. Finally, as Wang fails to remedy the failures of Baker, the Office Action does not cite Wang to teach the claimed battery.

For the above reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that the cited portions of Baker and Wang fail to disclose, teach, or suggest Claim 1 as amended herein. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of independent Claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 should be reconsidered and withdrawn. Additionally, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 2 to 10, which directly or indirectly, depend from independent Claim 1, are also allowable for the reasons given above with respect to Claim 1 and for the additional patentable features recited therein.

Furthermore, Applicant submits that independent Claim 11 includes similar patentable features to those discussed above with respect to independent Claim 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that amended Claim 11 is patentable over Baker and Wang for the same reasons as Claim 1. Lastly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 12 to 20, which depend directly or indirectly from independent Claim 11, are also allowable for the reasons given above with respect to Claims 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of Claims 11 to 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

For the foregoing reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that all of the present claims are allowable. In the event there remains any impediment to allowance of the claims, which could be clarified in a telephonic interview, the Examiner is respectfully requested to initiate such an interview with the undersigned. Additionally, if the Examiner has any questions regarding this Response, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner contact the undersigned.
Respectfully submitted,
K&L Gates LLP BY /Kevin T. McCormick/
